is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles gambiae s.l. (along with Anopheles pharoensis and Anopheles ziemanni), as described in Methods and Table 1 (page 5).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Tested for knockdown resistance (kdr) mutations using PCR-RFLP following Martinez-Torres et al. 1998 (Vgsc L995F / L1014F), as described on page 4 and Table 3.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 3 on page 8 provides exact genotype counts (SS, RS, RR), sample sizes, and kdr allelic frequencies for Anopheles gambiae s.l. collected across different net types in three localities.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from the field in three locations in Benin: Abomey-Takplikpo (Adjarra district), Bame (Zangnanado district), and Malanville (Malanville district) (page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: The study presents primary empirical field research investigating mosquito entry into torn LLINs and subsequent kdr genotyping (pages 2-4).

sub_country_location.evidence: Provides specific village/district locations with geographic coordinates: Abomey-Takplikpo (6°31'54"N, 2°39'56"E), Bame (7°16'46"N, 2°24'46"E), and Malanville (11°50'27"N, 3°24'08"E) (page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected over a 5-month period from April to August 2010 (page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Routine primary field study conducted by Centre de Recherche Entomologique de Cotonou (CREC) with no indication of data duplication.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and site data are fully presented in the main text and Table 3.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated mosquito entry into torn LLINs versus untreated nets across three bioclimatic regions in Benin in 2010. A total of 320 field-caught female Anopheles gambiae s.l. were genotyped for the Vgsc L1014F (L995F) kdr mutation, and complete genotype counts (SS, RS, RR) were reported across sites and net types.
